title: Instead & For: 代わりに, に代わって, 向き, 向け, だけ
description: Instead of / in exchange for, on behalf of, suitable for vs. made for, and だけ meaning 'as much as'.

points.title: 〜代わりに: instead of; in exchange for
points.summary: Noun + の + 代わりに / verb + 代わりに = instead of A; or 'in return for A'.
points.body:
- 肉**の代わりに**、魚を食べよう (fish instead of meat).
- 英語を教える**代わりに**、日本語を教えてもらった (in exchange for teaching English).
examples: {今日|きょう}は{肉|にく}の{代|か}わりに、{魚|さかな}を{食|た}べよう。
Let's have fish instead of meat today.

points.title: 〜に代わって: on behalf of, in place of
points.summary: Person + に代わって = acting for someone (formal). Kanji: 代わる (substitute), not 変わる (change).
points.body:
- 社長**に代わって**、部長が挨拶をした.
- 母**に代わって**私が料理を作った.

代わる = substitute; 変わる = change (a different verb!).
examples: {社長|しゃちょう}に{代|か}わって、{部長|ぶちょう}が{挨拶|あいさつ}をした。
The department head gave the speech on behalf of the president.

points.title: 〜向き: suitable for; facing
points.summary: Noun + 向き = suited to (naturally fits); also direction: 南向き (south-facing). Verb: 向いている = be suited.
points.body:
- 南**向き**の部屋 (a south-facing room).
- この仕事は私には**向いていない** (this job isn't suited to me).

**向き vs 向け:** 向き = happens to suit; 向け = made/designed for (a target group).
examples: {南|みなみ}{向|む}きの{部屋|へや}は{明|あか}るい。

points.title: 〜向け: aimed at, designed for
points.summary: Noun + 向け = made for a target group: 子供向けの本, 外国人向けの雑誌.
points.body:
- これは子供**向け**に作られた本だ.
- 外国人**向け**の日本語の雑誌.
examples: これは{子供|こども}{向|む}けに{作|つく}られた{本|ほん}だ。
This is a book made for children.

points.title: 〜だけ (2): as much as
points.summary: Verb (dictionary/potential) / な-adj + だけ = as much as possible / as much as you like: 好きなだけ, できるだけ.
points.body:
- 好きな**だけ**食べてください (eat as much as you like).
- できる**だけ**早く来てください (as early as possible).
examples: {好|す}きなだけ{食|た}べてください。
Please eat as much as you like.

questions.prompt: {今日|きょう}は{肉|にく}の（　）、{魚|さかな}を{食|た}べよう。
notes: の代わって isn't grammatical.
Without に, it can't connect to the clause.
の代わる isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: Let's have fish instead of meat today.

questions.prompt: {英語|えいご}を{教|おし}える（　）、{日本語|にほんご}を{教|おし}えてもらった。
notes: うちに = 'while'.
向け follows a noun ({子供|こども}{向|む}け), not a verb.
ために = 'in order to / because' — doesn't express an exchange.
questions.translation: In exchange for teaching English, I was taught Japanese.

questions.prompt: {社長|しゃちょう}（　）、{部長|ぶちょう}が{挨拶|あいさつ}をした。
questions.explanation: On behalf of: **に代わって** (代 = substitute).
notes: を代わって isn't the pattern.
が代わって would make the president the one substituting.
変わる means 'to change' — wrong kanji/verb.
questions.translation: The department head gave the speech on behalf of the president.

questions.prompt: {今日|きょう}は{母|はは}（　）、{私|わたし}が{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}った。
notes: によって = 'by / depending on'.
{母|はは}だけ = 'only mother' — it clashes with {私|わたし}が.
にとって = 'for (someone)'.
questions.translation: Today I cooked in place of my mother.

questions.prompt: {南|みなみ}（　）の{部屋|へや}は{明|あか}るい。
notes: 向こう = 'over there'.
南向かい isn't the word for facing.
南向け would mean 'made for the south'.

questions.prompt: {細|こま}かい{作業|さぎょう}は{私|わたし}には（　）。
questions.explanation: Not suited: 向く → **向いていない**.
notes: 向きていない isn't a form.
向ける = 'point (something) at' — wrong verb.
向かっていない = 'not heading toward'.
questions.translation: Detailed work isn't suited to me.

questions.prompt: これは{子供|こども}（　）に{作|つく}られた{本|ほん}だ。
notes: 向かって = 'facing / toward'.
向かい = 'opposite'.
代わりに needs の ({子供|こども}の代わりに) and means 'instead of'.
questions.translation: This is a book made for children.

questions.prompt: {外国人|がいこくじん}（　）の{日本語|にほんご}の{雑誌|ざっし}
notes: 向かうの isn't grammatical.
向けての is used in formal titles but not standard here.
向くの isn't grammatical.

questions.prompt: {好|す}きな（　）{食|た}べてください。
questions.explanation: As much as you like: **好きなだけ**.
notes: 向け follows a noun ({大人|おとな}{向|む}け).
しか needs a negative.
好きなばかり isn't a phrase.
questions.translation: Please eat as much as you like.

questions.prompt: できる（　）{早|はや}く{来|き}てください。
notes: できるしか isn't a phrase.
できる代わりに = 'in exchange for being able' — not 'as … as possible'.
できるばかり isn't a phrase.
questions.translation: Please come as early as possible.

questions.prompt: {父|ちち}が{忙|いそが}しいので、{代|か}わり（　）{私|わたし}が{行|い}きます。
notes: 代わりを = 'a substitute (object)' — e.g. お代わりをください.
代わりで isn't standard.
代わりが isn't the pattern.
questions.translation: My father is busy, so I'll go instead.

questions.prompt: この{番組|ばんぐみ}は{大人|おとな}（　）だ。
notes: 向かい = 'opposite'.
大人代わり isn't a phrase — 代わり means 'instead of'.
向かって = 'toward'.
questions.translation: This programme is aimed at adults.

questions.prompt: {食|た}べられる（　）{食|た}べてください。
questions.explanation: As much as possible: **〜られるだけ**.
notes: 向け follows a noun, not a verb.
しか needs a negative.
食べられるばかり isn't a phrase.
questions.translation: Please eat as much as you can.
